{{short description|American mathematician}}
[[File:3D Printing Guru, Laura Taalman.jpg|alt=|thumb|Laura Taalman in South Africa]]
'''Laura Anne Taalman''', also known as '''mathgrrl''', is an American mathematician known for her work on the [[mathematics of Sudoku]] and for her mathematical [[3D printing]] models. Her mathematical research concerns [[knot theory]] and [[Singular point of an algebraic variety|singular algebraic geometry]]; she is a professor of mathematics at [[James Madison University]].

==Life==
Taalman earned a bachelor's degree in mathematics from the [[University of Chicago]] in 1994.{{r|cv}} She completed her Ph.D. at [[Duke University]] in 2000; her dissertation, ''Monomial Generators for the Nash Sheaf of a Complete Resolution'', was supervised by William L. Pardon.{{r|cv|mgp}} On finishing her doctorate, she joined the James Madison faculty; she has also worked as the mathematician-in-residence at the [[National Museum of Mathematics]] in 2014–2015.{{r|cv}}
[[File:Borromean ring knitting.png|thumb|A knitted model of a [[Borromean ring]] that Laura Taalman displayed [[New York City]].]]

==3d printing==
[[File:3D Printing and Mathematics models.jpg|thumb|3D Printing and Mathematics models by Taalman]]
In 2013–2014, after becoming head of the 3d printing lab at James Madison University, Taalman set out on a project of printing one 3d model per day. Her models have included subjects from mathematics including knots, fractals, and snap-together polyhedra.{{r|eskin|librarians}}

==Books==
With Peter Kohn, Taalman is the author of a textbook ''Calculus''.{{r|tkc}} She is also the author of a different text, ''Calculus I with Integrated Precalculus''.

With [[Jason Rosenhouse]] (also a mathematics professor at James Madison University) she is the author of ''[[Taking Sudoku Seriously|Taking Sudoku Seriously: The Mathematics Behind the World’s Most Popular Pencil Puzzle]]''.{{r|tss}} She has also written a series of Sudoku puzzle books with Philip Riley.{{r|henle}}

==Awards and honors==
Taalman won the Trevor Evans Award of the [[Mathematical Association of America]] in 2003 for her work with [[Eugénie Hunsicker]] on the mathematics of [[modular design|modular architecture]].{{r|simple}}

In 2005, Taalman won the Henry L. Alder Award for Distinguished
Teaching by a Beginning College or
University Mathematics Faculty Member, given by the [[Mathematical Association of America]].{{r|mathfest}}

Her book ''Taking Sudoku Seriously'' was the 2012 winner of the [[PROSE Awards]] in the popular science and popular mathematics category.{{r|prose}}
